title: White balance, measured on the camera
body: White balance now works the way it does on the camera. A preset is an absolute light: Daylight under a warm bulb turns the picture orange, because the correction runs from the light the scene was actually lit by to the preset's light, not relative to auto white balance.

The presets were measured on my X-T3: one chart RAW converted at each preset and along a kelvin ladder from 3200 to 8300 K, then fitted through Fonder's own graph, with Daylight pinned to the camera's dial. Cloudy is derived, halfway between Daylight and Shade in mired.

Apple's kelvin and the camera's aren't on the same scale: the same RAW reads 5981 K in Core Image and 5026 K on the camera's dial, 31.8 mired apart, so every reading is moved onto the camera's scale first. The phone's live reading is used in the viewfinder, and a RAW's own as-shot light when it's imported.
The same day a seventh choice, **K**, made a fixed kelvin one tap away, so a camera recipe like “5200K, R+1 B−6” can be entered as written.

images.alt: A colour chart at 3200, 4000, 5600 and 8300 kelvin, the camera's renders above Fonder's.
images.caption: The kelvin ladder on DSCF6533: the camera's conversions (top) and Fonder with the same fixed kelvin (bottom). The cool end still runs a little bluer in Fonder.

images.alt: A colour chart under the Incandescent, Daylight and Shade presets, the camera's renders above Fonder's.
images.caption: The presets on the same RAW. On the neutral patches the camera and Fonder differ by 0.005–0.013 in OKLab a/b, against 0.02–0.07 between a preset and Daylight on the camera itself.
